sentences.en: Hey there, Shankar here.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是香卡。

sentences.en: Since we first published this episode
sentences.zh: 自从我们在2018年

sentences.en: with Francesca Gino in 2018,
sentences.zh: 首次发布这期与弗兰切斯卡·吉诺合作的节目以来，

sentences.en: other researchers have raised concerns
sentences.zh: 其他研究人员对她工作的真实性

sentences.en: about the integrity of her work.
sentences.zh: 提出了担忧。

sentences.en: In 2023, a group of scientists publicly alleged
sentences.zh: 2023年，一群科学家公开指控

sentences.en: that she had fabricated data in some of her studies.
sentences.zh: 她在部分研究中伪造了数据。

sentences.en: You can find more information about their analysis
sentences.zh: 你可以在 datacollada.org

sentences.en: at datacollada.org.
sentences.zh: 找到关于他们分析的更多信息。

sentences.en: Francesca Gino has denied the allegations.
sentences.zh: 弗兰切斯卡·吉诺否认了这些指控。

sentences.en: A number of her studies have been retracted
sentences.zh: 她的多项研究已被

sentences.en: by the journals that published them,
sentences.zh: 发表这些研究的学术期刊撤稿，

sentences.en: including a study about karaoke that is referenced in this episode.
sentences.zh: 其中包括本期节目中提及的一项关于卡拉OK的研究。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: A few years ago, social scientist Francesca Gino was browsing the shelves at her local bookstore
sentences.zh: 几年前，社会科学家弗兰切斯卡·吉诺正在当地书店的货架间浏览，

sentences.en: when she came across an unusual-looking book in the cooking section.
sentences.zh: 这时她在烹饪区偶然看到了一本外表奇特书。

sentences.en: This recipe book, they look a little bit different, and the title said,
sentences.zh: 这本食谱看起来有点不一样，书名叫作

sentences.en: Never Trust a Skinny Italian Chef.
sentences.zh: 《永远不要相信一个瘦子意大利厨师》。

sentences.en: And being Italian, I was very intrigued.
sentences.zh: 身为意大利人，我当时非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And as I flipped through the pages, it became clear that this was not your typical recipe book.
sentences.zh: 当我翻阅书页时，我清楚地意识到这不是一本普通的食谱。

sentences.en: The dishes were playful, quirky, and improbable.
sentences.zh: 这里的菜肴充满趣味、古怪且不可思议。

sentences.en: Snails were paired with coffee sauce.
sentences.zh: 蜗牛与咖啡酱搭配在一起。

sentences.en: Vealtang with charcoal powder.
sentences.zh: 小牛舌佐以木炭粉。

sentences.en: The recipes had titles like how to burn a sardine.
sentences.zh: 食谱的名字有诸如“如何烤焦沙丁鱼”之类，

sentences.en: And, oops, I dropped the lemon tart.
sentences.zh: 还有“哎呀，我把柠檬塔摔了”。

sentences.en: There were pictures of beautiful dishes.
sentences.zh: 书中还配有精美菜肴的图片。

sentences.en: Who could resist a dish called the crunchy part of the lasagna?
sentences.zh: 谁能抗拒一道名为“千层面酥脆的部分”的菜呢？

sentences.en: Now, if you know anything about Italians,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你对意大利人有所了解的话，

sentences.en: first of all, we have lots of rules when it comes to cooking.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们在烹饪方面有很多规矩。

sentences.en: And second, we really cherish our traditional dishes,
sentences.zh: 其次，我们非常珍视传统菜肴，

sentences.en: especially because they've been passed on for generations.
sentences.zh: 特别是这些菜肴已经代代相传。

sentences.en: But this chef, one of the most successful in the world,
sentences.zh: 但这位厨师——世界上最成功的厨师之一，

sentences.en: couldn't resist circling back to one big existential question.
sentences.zh: 却忍不住反复思考一个宏大的存在主义问题：

sentences.en: Why is it that we cook the dish in this way?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们非要用这种方式烹饪这道菜？

sentences.en: Why is it that we cook the dish in this way?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们非要用这种方式烹饪这道菜？

sentences.en: It's the kind of question Francesca loved.
sentences.zh: 正是这种问题让弗兰切斯卡爱不释手。

sentences.en: As a professor at Harvard Business School, she studies nonconformists,
sentences.zh: 作为哈佛商学院的教授，她专门研究不墨守成规的人，

sentences.en: specifically people who break the rules and end up in trouble.
sentences.zh: 具体来说就是那些打破常规最终惹上麻烦的人。

sentences.en: But now, standing at the bookstore, she wondered,
sentences.zh: 但此时此刻，站在书店里的她不禁琢磨：

sentences.en: Can defying norms lead to innovation?
sentences.zh: 挑战常规能带来创新吗？

sentences.en: Can letting go of tradition lead to the most sublime examples of creative thinking?
sentences.zh: 抛弃传统能催生出最精妙的创造性思维吗？

sentences.en: To find out, she got in touch with the man behind the cookbook,
sentences.zh: 为了找到答案，她联系了这本食谱背后的那个人，

sentences.en: the so-called Jimi Hendrix of Italian cooking, Massimo Battura.
sentences.zh: 也就是被称为意大利烹饪界“吉米·亨德里克斯”的马西莫·巴图拉。

sentences.en: After a few conversations, he said,
sentences.zh: 经过几次交谈，他说：

sentences.en: look, if you really want to understand the business, you got to come to Modena.
sentences.zh: 听着，如果你真的想了解这门生意，你得来摩德纳。

sentences.en: And I was like, of course.
sentences.zh: 当时我的反应是：当然去。

sentences.en: Why say no to an invitation to a three Michelin star restaurant?
sentences.zh: 怎么能拒绝米其林三星餐厅的邀请呢？

sentences.en: I'm on my way.
sentences.zh: 我这就出发。

sentences.en: This week, we'll revisit a favorite conversation with Francesca about her mission to understand the minds of successful nonconformists.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将重温与弗兰切斯卡的一次精彩对话，探讨她旨在理解成功叛逆者思维模式的使命。

sentences.en: I think we really need to shift our thinking.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们确实需要转变思维方式。

sentences.en: Rebels are not troublemakers.
sentences.zh: 反叛者不是麻烦制造者。

sentences.en: They're not outcasts.
sentences.zh: 他们不是被流放者。

sentences.en: Rebels are people who break rules that should be broken.
sentences.zh: 反叛者是那些打破本该打破的规则的人。

sentences.en: They break rules that hold them and others back.
sentences.zh: 他们打破那些束缚自己和他人的陈规陋习。

sentences.en: And their way of rule-breaking is constructive rather than destructive.
sentences.zh: 他们打破规则的方式是建设性的，而非破坏性的。

sentences.en: It creates positive change.
sentences.zh: 它能创造积极的改变。

sentences.en: Cultivating your inner rebel.
sentences.zh: 培养你內心的反叛精神。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看本周的“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Francesca Gino is a busy person.
sentences.zh: 弗兰切斯卡·吉诺是个大忙人。

sentences.en: She teaches at the Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 她在哈佛商学院教书。

sentences.en: She's a prolific researcher and writer.
sentences.zh: 她是一位高产的研究员和作家。

sentences.en: She advises corporations and non-profit organizations on decision-making and negotiations.
sentences.zh: 她为企业和非营利组织提供决策和谈判方面的咨询。

sentences.en: So she has no shortage of things on her to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，她的待办事项清单上永远排满了各种事情。

sentences.en: But when chef Massimo Bottura offered her the chance to watch him in action at his restaurant,
sentences.zh: 但当主厨马西莫·巴图拉邀请她去餐厅观摩他工作时，

sentences.en: she knew she needed to hop on a plane and go to Italy.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己必须立刻坐上飞机前往意大利。

sentences.en: So I showed up at the restaurant for my first day with my notebook,
sentences.zh: 于是第一天我带着笔记本出现在餐厅，

sentences.en: and basically I was given an apron.
sentences.zh: 基本上我被发了一件围裙。

sentences.en: For the entire day, I was put to work in the front of the house as a server.
sentences.zh: 整整一天，我都作为服务员被安排在前厅工作。

sentences.en: And again, it was an amazing experience because I had no qualification.
sentences.zh: 再次说明，这是一次奇妙的经历，因为我没有任何资格。

sentences.en: I clearly didn't know what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 我显然不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: I made a lot of mistakes.
sentences.zh: 我犯了很多错误。

sentences.en: But that was just an example of doing things a little bit differently.
sentences.zh: 但这只是用略有不同的方式做事的一个例子。

sentences.en: So, of course, if you're a smart chef, the one thing you don't do is bring an amateur into your three Michelin star restaurant and ask her to start serving the dishes.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然了，如果你是一个明智的厨师，你绝对不会做的一件事就是把一个业余爱好者带进你的米其林三星餐厅，并让她开始上菜。

sentences.en: I can just imagine all the ways that that could go wrong.
sentences.zh: 我完全可以想象这会出多少差错。

sentences.en: Did it?
sentences.zh: 真的出了吗？

sentences.en: That is exactly what was going through my head as I was making mistakes
sentences.zh: 这正是我把那些精心摆盘的菜肴端上桌时，

sentences.en: from putting the very carefully arranged dishes down onto the table.
sentences.zh: 脑子里一直在想的事情。

sentences.en: There are very specific ways in which the dish gets arranged
sentences.zh: 菜肴的摆盘有着非常具体的要求，

sentences.en: so that you get the right anticipation of what the dish is going to be about as you eat it.
sentences.zh: 这样当你品尝时，就能对这道菜的风味产生正确的期待。

sentences.en: And throughout the day, the team members were working with me in the front of the house,
sentences.zh: 在这一整天里，在前厅和我一起工作的团队成员

sentences.en: were just helping me.
sentences.zh: 一直在帮助我。

sentences.en: And when I was making mistakes, they were very subtly trying to correct, so they were adjusting the plate, or if I brought to a table the wrong utensils,
sentences.zh: 当我犯错时，他们会非常巧妙地试图纠正：他们会调整盘子的位置，或者如果我拿错了餐具去某个桌子，

sentences.en: they would show up and somehow bring another set that was the rice set for the type of dish that was being served.
sentences.zh: 他们就会出现，不知怎么地带来一套适合正在供应的那道菜的饭碗。

sentences.en: So I understand that if I were to visit the restaurant, I might sometimes see Massimo Bottura outside unloading produce from the trucks or sweeping the pavement.
sentences.zh: 所以我了解到，如果我去那家餐厅参观，有时可能会看到马西莫·巴图拉在外面从卡车上卸下农产品，或者在扫马路。

sentences.en: He doesn't seem like someone who stands on airs.
sentences.zh: 他看起来一点也不摆架子。

sentences.en: He's very much into the trenches.
sentences.zh: 他非常亲力亲为、深入基层。

sentences.en: One of the first things that he does when he shows up at the restaurant in the morning is to put his white chef's coat on.
sentences.zh: 他早上来到餐厅后做的第一件事就是穿上白色的厨师服。

sentences.en: And then he does go outside with a broom and sweep the streets.
sentences.zh: 然后他真的会拿着扫帚走到外面去扫街。

sentences.en: And you're there looking at him and the sous chef and the people working in the restaurants are there looking at him.
sentences.zh: 你站在那儿看着他，副主厨和餐厅里工作的人也都站在那儿看着他。

sentences.en: And you ask the question, why is it that he's doing that?
sentences.zh: 你会心生疑问：他为什么要做这些？

sentences.en: But the second question that you ask yourself is, why is it that I'm not doing it?
sentences.zh: 但你问自己的第二个问题是：为什么我没有这样做？

sentences.en: And so you're feeling motivated to take on roles and activities that are roles that are not scripted because of where you sit or where you work in the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 于是你会感到有动力去承担那些并非按部就班的角色和活动——这些角色并非因为你在餐厅的位置或工作而预先规定好的。

sentences.en: It's very refreshing.
sentences.zh: 这感觉非常耳目一新。

sentences.en: And, of course, he actually tries to bring this approach to the food that he's making as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，他实际上也试图将这种方法运用到他制作的食物中。

sentences.en: I want you to listen to this clip of music because you say the chef actually asked his staff to build a dish based on this song.
sentences.zh: 我想让你听听这段音乐剪辑，因为你说这位厨师实际上要求他的员工根据这首歌创作一道菜。

sentences.en: Holly came from Miami, F.L.A.
sentences.zh: 霍莉来自佛罗里达州迈阿密，

sentences.en: Hitchhiked her way across the U.S.A.
sentences.zh: 一路搭便车横穿美国，

sentences.en: Plucked her eyebrows on the way.
sentences.zh: 途中还修剪了眉毛。

sentences.en: Shaved her legs and then he was a she.
sentences.zh: 刮了腿毛，然后他变成了她。

sentences.en: She says, hey babe, take a walk on the wild side
sentences.zh: 她说，嘿，宝贝，去走一走狂野之路。

sentences.en: Said, hey honey, take a walk on the wild side
sentences.zh: 说，嘿，亲爱的，去走一走狂野之路。

sentences.en: So what was going on, Francesca?
sentences.zh: 那么当时是怎么回事，弗兰切斯卡？

sentences.en: How do you make a dish based on a song?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能根据一首歌做出道菜呢？

sentences.en: It was one of the many ways that Massimo Bottura inspires the people working in the kitchen
sentences.zh: 这是马西莫·巴图拉激励厨房员工的众多方法之一，

sentences.en: and really asks them to bring out their own contribution and their own voices.
sentences.zh: 他真心要求他们发挥自己的贡献、发出自己的声音。

sentences.en: So you would see him walk into the kitchen and say,
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到他走进厨房说：

sentences.en: Lou Reed, walk to the outside.
sentences.zh: 娄·里德，《走向野外》。

sentences.en: or a different name of a song or a different poem
sentences.zh: 或者是一首不同歌曲的名字，或是一首不同的诗，

sentences.en: or the name of a phrase of something that he was reading recently
sentences.zh: 或者是他最近读到的某个短语，

sentences.en: or the name of a piece of art that he saw at an art show.
sentences.zh: 又或者是他在艺术展上看到的一件艺术品的名称。

sentences.en: And what he's trying to do is asking people to think about how that song
sentences.zh: 他试图做的是让人们思考那首歌

sentences.en: or how that piece of art inspired them to come up with their own dish.
sentences.zh: 或那件艺术品如何启发他们做出自己的菜肴。

sentences.en: And what he's trying to do at the very core
sentences.zh: 而他核心的意图

sentences.en: is making sure that people don't show up at work
sentences.zh: 是确保人们来到工作岗位时

sentences.en: and somehow they leave their identity at the door,
sentences.zh: 不会把自己的身份抛在门外，

sentences.en: but rather they show up and they're being who they are.
sentences.zh: 而是带着本色来到这里，展现真实的自我。

sentences.en: They're bringing their ideas forward, their contributions forward,
sentences.zh: 他们提出自己的想法，做出自己的贡献，

sentences.en: independent of their background, their nationalities,
sentences.zh: 而不受其背景、国籍

sentences.en: or how much training they have.
sentences.zh: 或接受过多少培训的限制。

sentences.en: And when you spoke to the staff at the restaurant,
sentences.zh: 当你和餐厅的员工交谈时，

sentences.en: what did they say the role of the chef was in inspiring them?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么评价主厨在启发他们方面所扮演的角色的？

sentences.en: Did they actually agree that these techniques were actually bringing out the best in them?
sentences.zh: 他们真的认同这些技巧确实激发了他们最好的一面吗？

sentences.en: What the staff said, which is really interesting, is that Massimo is the type of leader who never says hi, hi, hi, hi.
sentences.zh: 员工们说了一件非常有趣的事：马西莫从来不是那种高高在上的领导。

sentences.en: It's always about the we.
sentences.zh: 他总是强调“我们”。

sentences.en: He describes the restaurant as a crew or as a ship.
sentences.zh: 他把餐厅形容为一个船员集体或一艘船。

sentences.en: In fact, he often talks about being on a pirate ship.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他经常谈到自己身处一艘海盗船上。

sentences.en: And sometimes the waters out there are going to be turbulent.
sentences.zh: 有时外面的水域会波涛汹涌。

sentences.en: But for the very fact that we are going to bring out our individual contributions, but we're going to do so being aware that we are part of a team,
sentences.zh: 但正因为我们要发挥各自的贡献，同时又深知我们是一个团队，

sentences.en: no matter how terrible in the sea is, we're going to succeed.
sentences.zh: 无论海面多么恶劣，我们都一定会成功。

sentences.en: And people do feel very inspired by the way he leads the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 人们确实被他领导餐厅的方式深深启发。

sentences.en: Here's another thing that makes Massimo a rebel.
sentences.zh: 让马西莫成为反叛者的另一件事是：

sentences.en: He asks a lot of questions about why things are the way they are.
sentences.zh: 他会对现状提出许多“为什么”。

sentences.en: For Francesca, a fearless curiosity is at the heart of rebel talent.
sentences.zh: 对弗兰切斯卡来说，无所畏惧的好奇心是反叛天赋的核心。

sentences.en: Bottura opened up a restaurant by asking the question, why not?
sentences.zh: 巴图拉开办餐厅时，问出的第一个问题就是：为什么不呢？

sentences.en: He had no experience in running a restaurant, let alone cooking, because he didn't go to culinary school.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何经营餐厅的经验，更不用说烹饪了，因为他没有上过厨艺学校。

sentences.en: He was in law school.
sentences.zh: 他当时在读法学院。

sentences.en: He was there for two years as a way to stick to what his father wanted.
sentences.zh: 他在那里呆了两年，只是为了顺从他父亲的意愿，

sentences.en: and then he didn't enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 但他并不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And when his brother, one of these brothers,
sentences.zh: 当他的兄弟——其中一位兄弟——

sentences.en: told him about this restaurant that was up for sale,
sentences.zh: 告诉他有一家餐厅正在出售时，

sentences.en: he really asked himself the question, why not?
sentences.zh: 他真的问了自己这个问题：为什么不呢？

sentences.en: That's curiosity.
sentences.zh: 这就是好奇心。

sentences.en: We are so often focused on efficiency and getting things done.
sentences.zh: 我们常常专注于效率和把事情做完。

sentences.en: We have a very long to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 我们的待办事项清单非常长。

sentences.en: But what that often comes at the cost of is allowing us to explore.
sentences.zh: 但这往往以牺牲我们探索的能力为代价。

sentences.en: The way we used to when we were a very little kid,
sentences.zh: 就像我们小时候那样，

sentences.en: And that came very naturally to us.
sentences.zh: 那种好奇心对我们来说是极其自然的。

sentences.en: So I see too many leaders who focus so much on efficiency that curiosity shut down in people.
sentences.zh: 所以我看到太多领导者过于关注效率，以至于人们的好奇心都被扼杀了。

sentences.en: And that's too bad because curiosity leads to all sorts of great results and great outcomes.
sentences.zh: 这太遗憾了，因为好奇心会带来各种各样的丰硕成果和美好结局。

sentences.en: There's a tension that runs through much of the book.
sentences.zh: 这本书通篇贯穿着一种张力。

sentences.en: And the tension is the tension between expertise and experimentation.
sentences.zh: 这种张力就是专业知识与尝试创新之间的张力。

sentences.en: And I want to come back and talk about this over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我想回过头来，一遍又一遍地探讨这个话题。

sentences.en: But I also want to do it through the lens of another story that you explore.
sentences.zh: 但我也想通过你探讨的另一个故事来切入。

sentences.en: you've looked at the story of Captain Chesley Sullenberger,
sentences.zh: 你研究过切斯利·萨伦伯格机长的故事，

sentences.en: better known as Captain Sully.

sentences.zh: 我想这是我从你刚才的话中获得的感悟之一。

sentences.en: Having a mix of people in the room who look at things from different perspectives could just be inherently valuable.
sentences.zh: 在团队中汇聚一群从不同视角看待事物的人，本身就可能具有巨大的价值。

sentences.en: Having people who look at the problem from a very different perspective is, in fact, a key to solving tough probleMs.
sentences.zh: 让那些从截然不同的视角看待问题的人参与进来，实际上正是解决棘手问题的关键。

sentences.en: But the reality is that many of us don't want to be challenged.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，我们当中许多人并不想接受挑战。

sentences.en: It's so much easier to go through life, whether at work or at home for that matter,
sentences.zh: 生活要轻松得多，无论是在工作中还是在家里，

sentences.en: with people that just nod their heads and say, yep, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 只要周围的人对你点头哈腰，说：“没错，我同意你的看法。”

sentences.en: But rebel leaders and rebel employees are people who really try to surround themselves
sentences.zh: 但反叛的领袖和反叛的员工，是那些真正试图让自己周围

sentences.en: with people who think differently and with people who do challenge them.
sentences.zh: 环绕着那些思维不同、敢于挑战他们的人。

sentences.en: I asked Francesca about another rebel she mentions in her book, the filmmaker Ava DuVernay.
sentences.zh: 我问了弗兰西斯卡关于她书中提到的另一个反叛者，电影制作人阿娃·杜威内。

sentences.en: You might be familiar with her work in movies such as Selma,
sentences.zh: 你可能对她的电影作品很熟悉，比如《塞尔玛》，

sentences.en: an account of a series of famous civil rights marches
sentences.zh: 那是一部关于一系列著名民权游行的记述，

sentences.en: led by Martin Luther King Jr.
sentences.zh: 由小马丁·路德·金领导，

sentences.en: That means proteSt.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着抗议。

sentences.en: That means march.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着游行。

sentences.en: That means disturb the peace.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着打破平静。

sentences.en: That means jail.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着入狱。

sentences.en: That means risk.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着冒险。

sentences.en: And you say that her story reveals another really important idea
sentences.zh: 你说她的故事揭示了另一个非常重要的想法，

sentences.en: when it comes to rebel talent,
sentences.zh: 当谈到反叛天才时，

sentences.en: which is the importance of being vigilant to stereotypes,
sentences.zh: 那就是警惕刻板印象的重要性，

sentences.en: to recognize that stereotypes can actually serve
sentences.zh: 认识到刻板印象实际上可以充当

sentences.en: as a kind of straitjacket that prevents us from thinking creatively?
sentences.zh: 一种紧身衣，阻碍我们的创造性思维？

sentences.en: In all sorts of spheres of life, we are affected by stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 在生活的各个领域，我们都受到刻板印象的影响。

sentences.en: Or more generally, we accept social roles that others have passed on to us.
sentences.zh: 或者更笼统地说，我们接受了别人传给我们的社会角色。

sentences.en: And the story of Ava DuVernay is a beautiful one because she just doesn't do that.
sentences.zh: 阿娃·杜威内的故事非常美妙，因为她偏不这样。

sentences.en: And this comes from a person who decided to go to filmmaking later in her career.
sentences.zh: 而这来自于一个在职业生涯后期才决定从事电影制作的人。

sentences.en: She was doing a different job and she said, I'm going to switch and enter this job.
sentences.zh: 她当时做着别的工作，然后说：“我要转行，进入这个行业。”

sentences.en: And in the advice that she was receiving from others, everybody was talking about the importance of really being supported by others, reaching out to networks.
sentences.zh: 在听取别人的建议时，每个人都在谈论获得他人支持、拓展人脉网络的重要性。

sentences.en: She didn't have that.
sentences.zh: 她没有这些。

sentences.en: And she just started picking up the camera and working on her own movies.
sentences.zh: 她只是拿起摄像机，开始拍摄自己的电影。

sentences.en: And in fact, the first films she created were supported by her own savings.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她创作的第一部电影是用自己的积蓄支持的。

sentences.en: And then she became known for the work that she was doing, for the fact that she was not accepting the rules of the business, but in a sense,
sentences.zh: 然后，她因自己的作品而闻名，因为她不接受这个行业的规则，从某种意义上说，

sentences.en: she was working and fighting against them.
sentences.zh: 她在与它们抗争并努力打破它们。

sentences.en: And it's quite amazing and inspiring as a story.
sentences.zh: 作为一个故事，这相当惊人且鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: And so for me, I made my first film, my first feature film when I was 38.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，我38岁时制作了我的第一部电影，我的第一部剧情片。

sentences.en: So it's never too late that I just started from the outside.
sentences.zh: 所以永远不会太迟，我只是从局外开始。

sentences.en: Rebels constructively break the rules.
sentences.zh: 反叛者具有建设性地打破规则。

sentences.en: They push ahead even when they don't have the support of power brokers.
sentences.zh: 即使没有权力大亨的支持，他们也会勇往直前。

sentences.en: And once they achieve success, they continue to think like beginners
sentences.zh: 一旦成功，他们仍会像初学者一样思考，

sentences.en: and go out of their way to learn from those who disagree with them.
sentences.zh: 并刻意向那些意见相左的人学习。

sentences.en: So how can you activate your inner nonconformist?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何唤醒你内心的不守常规者呢？

sentences.en: That's when we come back.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们再谈。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Today we're talking about rebels.
sentences.zh: 今天我们来聊聊反叛者。

sentences.en: people who break free of social norms and achieve incredible feats of imagination.
sentences.zh: 那些挣脱社会规范、取得惊人想象力成就的人。

sentences.en: Why is this something so few of us do?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们中很少有人这么做？

sentences.en: One problem is that we know too much.
sentences.zh: 一个问题是，我们知道得太多了。

sentences.en: We become experts in our fields and then fall back on familiar routines.
sentences.zh: 我们成为了各自领域的专家，然后便退守到熟悉的常规中。

sentences.en: We forget how to see the world with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记了如何用崭新的眼光看待世界。

sentences.en: But it doesn't have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 但事情并非一定如此。

sentences.en: Francesca Gino says that being a rebel is a skill that all of us can cultivate.
sentences.zh: 弗兰西斯卡·吉诺说，做个反叛者是我们所有人都可以培养的一种技能。

sentences.en: Sometimes it takes only small steps.
sentences.zh: 有时，这只需要迈出一小步。

sentences.en: A few years ago, she wondered if getting people to feel comfortable about being uncomfortable could be the first step in activating their inner rebel.
sentences.zh: 几年前，她想知道，让人习惯不舒服是否能成为唤醒他们内心反叛者的第一步。

sentences.en: She asked students to stand before their friends and classmates and sing Don't Stop Believing by Journey.
sentences.zh: 她让学生们站在朋友和同学面前，演唱旅行乐队的《不要停止信仰》。

sentences.en: Can you set up the experiment for me, Francesca?
sentences.zh: 弗兰西斯卡，你能为我介绍一下这个实验吗？

sentences.en: I'm putting my hand in my hair as I was reminded when I was running this study.
sentences.zh: 当我想起自己做这项研究的时候，我正把手插在头发里。

sentences.en: This was a study that was inspired by the notion that when we break rules, when we break away from what other people expect of us, we feel a sense of confidence.
sentences.zh: 这项研究的灵感来自于这样一个观点：当我们打破规则，当我们脱离别人的期望时，我们会产生一种自信感。

sentences.en: And so to test that, I brought undergraduates to the lab and I asked them to engage in the task that you just heard.
sentences.zh: 为了测试这一点，我把大学生带到实验室，让他们完成你刚才听到的任务。

sentences.en: Stand up in front of a video with a microphone and in front of other participants watching you singing Don't Stop Believing.
sentences.zh: 站在摄像机和一个麦克风前，在其他参与者的注视下演唱《不要停止信仰》。

sentences.en: That was one of the songs.
sentences.zh: 那是其中一首歌。

sentences.en: And some of the participants did just that, but some others were asked to wear a bandana as they were singing, something that they told me made them uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 一些参与者照做了，但另一些人被要求在唱歌时戴上头巾，他们告诉我这让他们感到不舒服。

sentences.en: And then I was interested in seeing whether the anxiety and stress that they experienced during the task and their level of confidence, in addition to their performance,
sentences.zh: 然后我很想看看他们在任务中经历的焦虑和压力以及他们的自信水平，除了他们的表现之外，

sentences.en: was going to be different in these two different conditions.
sentences.zh: 在这两种不同的条件下是否会有所不同。

sentences.en: And it was both looking at physiological measure of stress, but also their self-reported measures in answering the question of how confident they felt.
sentences.zh: 这不仅要看压力的生理指标，还要看他们在回答关于自己有多自信的问题时的自我报告指标。

sentences.en: People who were wearing the bandana while they were singing in front of their peers felt more confident, felt less stress.
sentences.zh: 在同伴面前唱歌时戴着头巾的人表现得更自信，压力也更小。

sentences.en: So despite the fact that they thought they would feel more uncomfortable and that it would be harder for them,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管他们原以为自己会感到更不舒服、会更难熬，

sentences.en: The fact that they were wearing their bandana, something that the peers didn't expect, was actually helpful to them.
sentences.zh: 但他们戴着头巾——这是同伴们意料之外的事情——实际上对他们有所帮助。

sentences.en: And this is not just their feelings and their physiology.
sentences.zh: 这不仅体现在他们的感觉和生理上。

sentences.en: When you look at the performance in terms of how much they stay on tune, since the karaoke was recording that objectively, they did better.
sentences.zh: 当你从他们是否唱准音调的角度来看待表现时，由于卡拉OK客观地记录了这一点，他们表现得更好。

sentences.en: So there's a paradox here, because in the one case, you're asking one set of students to sing the song, which is clearly difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一个悖论，因为在第一种情况下，你让一组学生唱这首歌，这显然很难，

sentences.en: and especially before your friends in a classroom, it's difficult to do.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在教室里的朋友面前，这很难做到。

sentences.en: But the second group is being asked to do something even more difficult.
sentences.zh: 但第二组被要求做更难的事情。

sentences.en: You're asking them to sing the song and also wear this non-conforming, you know, headdress.
sentences.zh: 你让他们唱这首歌，还要戴上这种非传统的头饰。

sentences.en: And you would think that the second group would do worse, but you found exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为第二组会表现得更差，但你发现的结果却恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Oftentimes we think that breaking rules is going to lead to worse outcomes
sentences.zh: 通常我们认为打破规则会导致更糟的结果，

sentences.en: and it's going to make us feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 而且会让我们感到不舒服。

sentences.en: And it does to a certain extent, but it then turns into confidence.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上确实如此，但它随后会转化为自信。

sentences.en: And that confidence translates in better performance.
sentences.zh: 而这种自信会转化为更好的表现。

sentences.en: It is paradoxical, but it's one of the big lessons in being rebelliousness.
sentences.zh: 这很矛盾，但这是叛逆行为带来的重要教训之一。

sentences.en: It does pay off.
sentences.zh: 它确实会有所回报。

sentences.en: I understand that you've discovered this about yourself as well.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你对你自己也有这样的发现。

sentences.en: You've run experiments of a sort where you try on the effects of different kinds of footwear
sentences.zh: 你做过某种实验，尝试穿不同类型的鞋子，

sentences.en: and the effects it has on your audiences.
sentences.zh: 以及它对你的观众产生的影响。

sentences.en: One time I was asked to teach two classes, the same class, back to back.
sentences.zh: 有一次我被要求连续上两堂课，内容完全一样。

sentences.en: And in each class I had 110 executives.
sentences.zh: 每堂课都有110名高管。

sentences.en: And since I was teaching the same content across the two classes,
sentences.zh: 既然我在两堂课上教的内容完全一样，

sentences.en: what I thought I could do is change my shoes in between the two classes.
sentences.zh: 我想我可以做的是在两堂课之间换鞋。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what I did.
sentences.zh: 我确实也这么做了。

sentences.en: So picture this professor dressed up in a really nice suit.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下这个教授穿着一身非常漂亮的西装。

sentences.en: And for the first class, I was wearing formal leather shoes, probably what the students expected from an HBS professor or a professor in general teaching in exec ed.
sentences.zh: 在上第一节课时，我穿着正式的皮鞋，这大概是学生们对哈佛商学院教授或一般在高级管理教育中授课的教授的期望。

sentences.en: But for the second class, I changed out my leather shoes for a pair of red sneakers.
sentences.zh: 但到了第二堂课，我把皮鞋换成了一双红运动鞋。

sentences.en: And it was interesting to walk to class.
sentences.zh: 走进教室时感觉很有意思。

sentences.en: My colleagues were giving me the strange look, thinking what it is that she's doing.
sentences.zh: 我的同事们用奇怪的眼神看着我，心想她在搞什么名堂。

sentences.en: And I was going to teach my second class.
sentences.zh: 然后我去上我的第二节课。

sentences.en: And at the end of each of the two classes, I gave the executives a little survey.
sentences.zh: 在这两堂课结束后，我给高管们做了一个小调查。

sentences.en: And in the survey, I was asking them questions like, how much do you think I charge for my consulting?
sentences.zh: 在调查中，我问了他们一些问题，比如，你认为我的咨询费收多少？

sentences.en: How much influence do you think I have at HBS as a professor?
sentences.zh: 你认为我作为教授在哈佛商学院有多大的影响力？

sentences.en: How often do you think I publish in a practitioner-oriented magazine like Harvard Business Review?
sentences.zh: 你认为我多久在像《哈佛商业评论》这样面向实践者的杂志上发表一次文章？

sentences.en: And what was interesting is that these are measures that capture how much influence the student thought I had.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这些指标反映了学生认为我有多大的影响力。

sentences.en: And what the survey results showed is that they had higher respect.
sentences.zh: 调查结果显示，他们表现出更高的尊重。

sentences.en: They thought of me as a more influential person when I taught them the same content, just wearing red sneakers.
sentences.zh: 当我给他们讲授同样的内容、只是脚上穿着红运动鞋时，他们认为我是个更有影响力的人。

sentences.en: So, of course,
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，

sentences.en: people listening to this are going to go out and get red sneakers and wear bandanas to work tomorrow because that's what you're saying is going to get them taken more seriously.
sentences.zh: 听到这里的人明天就会跑去买红运动鞋，戴着头巾去上班，因为这就是你所说能让他们变得更受重视的方法。

sentences.en: I recently did a training for a company around the issues of rebel talent and the people who invited me out were all in a team wearing red sneakers and they got a lot of compliments and questions throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 我最近为一家公司做了一场关于反叛天才问题的培训，邀请我去的那些人整个团队都穿着红运动鞋，他们整天都得到了很多赞美和提问。

sentences.en: So, yes, that could be one of the lessons learned out of this research.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这可能是从这项研究中吸取的教训之一。

sentences.en: Another way we can all get better at breaking the rules is to stay mindful of the things happening around us.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都能更好地打破规则的另一个方法是，对周围发生的事情保持觉察。

sentences.en: Sometimes we're so focused on the job at hand that we fail to see how the situation might afford us opportunities to demonstrate leadership and authenticity.
sentences.zh: 有时我们太专注于手头的工作，以至于看不到情况如何为我们提供展现领导力和真实自我的机会。

sentences.en: Maurice Cheeks had such an opportunity on April 25, 2003, during the NBA playoffs.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯·奇克斯在2003年4月25日的NBA季后赛中就遇到了这样的机会。

sentences.en: Maurice was coach of the Portland Trailblazers, and his team was down 2-0 in the series.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯是波特兰开拓者队的教练，他的球队在系列赛中以0比2落后。

sentences.en: It was a high-stakes moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个千钧一发的时刻。

sentences.en: And now to honor America and salute the men and women serving our country with our national anthem.
sentences.zh: 现在请奏国歌，以表彰美国并向为国效力的军人致敬。

sentences.en: 20,000 excited basketball fans are in the Rose Garden in Portland.
sentences.zh: 2万名兴奋的篮球迷聚集在波特兰的玫瑰花园球馆。

sentences.en: The crowd falls silent as a nervous-looking 13-year-old girl walks toward the microphone.
sentences.zh: 人群安静下来，一个看起来很紧张的13岁女孩走向麦克风。

sentences.en: Please welcome, as voted by you, the fans, our winner of the Toyota Get the Feeling of a Star promotion, Natalie Gilbert.
sentences.zh: 请欢迎由你们——球迷们投票选出的丰田“感受明星”活动获胜者，娜塔莉·吉尔伯特。

sentences.en: Oh, say can you see
sentences.zh: 噢，你可看见

sentences.en: At first, things go well.
sentences.zh: 起初，一切顺利。

sentences.en: Natalie looks confident, relaxed.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉看起来很自信、很放松。

sentences.en: And as you can hear, she is making a mistake.
sentences.zh: 正如你所听到的，她出错了。

sentences.en: She's looking for her father to get some support.
sentences.zh: 她在寻找父亲以获得一些支持。

sentences.en: And then somebody shows up to help her.
sentences.zh: 然后有人出现来帮她。

sentences.en: It's Maurice Cheeks.
sentences.zh: 那就是莫里斯·奇克斯。

sentences.en: At a moment when you might think that all his attention would be focused on his team
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，你可能会认为他的全部注意力都集中在球队

sentences.en: and their chances in the game,
sentences.zh: 以及他们在比赛中的胜算上，

sentences.en: Maurice has the presence of mind to realize that a child is in trouble.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯却心细如发地意识到一个孩子遇到了麻烦。

sentences.en: He has a daughter about Natalie's age.
sentences.zh: 他有一个和娜塔莉差不多大的女儿。

sentences.en: He rushes up to stand beside her.
sentences.zh: 他冲过去站在她身边。

sentences.en: He drapes an arm around her and says,
sentences.zh: 他把一只胳膊搭在她肩上说：

sentences.en: Come on, come on.
sentences.zh: “加油，加油。”

sentences.en: Natalie hesitates.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉犹豫了一下。

sentences.en: She doesn't know this stranger in the gray suit who has come up to stand by her side.
sentences.zh: 她不认识这个穿着灰色西装、走过来站在她身边的陌生人。

sentences.en: But Maurice Cheeks is now singing, and Natalie is lifted along.
sentences.zh: 但莫里斯·奇克斯现在正唱着，娜塔莉也受到了鼓舞。

sentences.en: Natalie looks confident again.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉再次看起来很自信。

sentences.en: Her voice soars.
sentences.zh: 她的歌声高亢起来。

sentences.en: And then something happens in the stadium.
sentences.zh: 接着，体育场里发生了变化。

sentences.en: Thousands of fans, the players, they see what Maurice has done.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的球迷、球员们，都看到了莫里斯的所作所为。

sentences.en: And now, everyone is singing.
sentences.zh: 现在，每个人都在合唱。

sentences.en: It is triumphant.
